visual.prompt: Educational infographic: Dramatic space view of our Sun as a glowing golden orb against the black of space. Visible solar flares and corona extending outward. Earth shown tiny in corner for scale reference. Warm golden light rays emanating outward. Text overlay: 'Our Star'. Cinematic 8K quality, photorealistic NASA-style visualization with educational diagram aesthetic.
visual.reasoning: Opens with awe-inspiring cosmic perspective to immediately capture attention and establish the scale and importance of our star.

kelly.pose: welcoming stance, arms open, looking up with wonder
kelly.expression: amazed wonder, wide eyes, delighted smile

visual.prompt: Kelly teaching about light travel from the Sun. Background: Split visualization showing the Sun on left, Earth on right, with a golden light beam connecting them across 93 million miles of space. Timer graphic showing '8 minutes' travel time. Starfield background. Educational overlay showing distance: '93,000,000 miles'. 8K cinematic quality.
visual.textOverlay: Light travels 93 million miles in just 8 minutes
visual.reasoning: Visualizes the abstract concept of light speed and distance in a tangible, memorable way.

kelly.pose: pointing gesture toward diagram, engaged teaching stance

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Stylized stopwatch showing 8 minutes, golden sun rays behind it, representing the incredibly fast speed of light. Bold text '8 Minutes!' at bottom. Clean educational style, warm golden tones.
optionA.responseScript: Exactly! Light is the fastest thing in the universe, traveling at 186,000 miles per second. Even at that incredible speed, it takes 8 whole minutes to reach us!

optionB.text: That seems slow for something so bright
optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Confused looking clock with question marks, gentle neutral styling. Bold text 'Seems Slow?' at bottom. Clean educational style.
optionB.responseScript: I get that! But remember, the Sun is 93 MILLION miles away. Light is actually traveling at 186,000 miles per second - the fastest anything can go in the universe!

visual.prompt: Educational infographic: Dramatic scale comparison showing the enormous Sun filling most of the frame, with a million tiny Earth spheres arranged inside it to show relative size. Clean visualization with size labels. Text: '1 Million Earths Could Fit Inside'. 8K quality, photorealistic planetary rendering, educational diagram aesthetic.
visual.reasoning: Mind-blowing scale comparison makes the abstract size tangible and memorable.

kelly.pose: both hands spread wide to emphasize vastness
kelly.expression: animated amazement, eyes wide with wonder

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Giant glowing sun with tiny Earth spheres floating inside it, showing incredible scale difference. Bold text 'MASSIVE!' at bottom. Clean educational style, subtle green glow border.
optionA.responseScript: Mind-blowing, right? The Sun is so big that if you could drive a car around it at highway speed, it would take about 5 years to make one lap!

optionB.text: How do we even measure that?
optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Ruler and measuring tools floating in space near celestial objects. Bold text 'How To Measure?' at bottom. Clean educational style.
optionB.responseScript: Great question! Scientists use the Sun's diameter - 864,000 miles across - and compare it to Earth's 7,918 miles. When you do the math with volumes, you get about 1.3 million Earths!

visual.prompt: Educational infographic: Cross-section of the Sun's core showing nuclear fusion in action. Hydrogen atoms combining to form helium with brilliant energy release. Energy waves radiating outward through layers. Text overlay: '4 Million Tons Per Second'. Scientific diagram style with glowing plasma effects. 8K quality, dramatic lighting.
visual.textOverlay: Converting 4 Million Tons to Energy Every Second
visual.reasoning: Reveals the hidden power source of the Sun in a visually compelling way.

kelly.pose: hands together then expanding outward, mimicking energy release

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Brilliant fusion reaction with hydrogen atoms combining, energy explosion radiating outward. Bold text 'Fusion Power!' at bottom. Clean educational style, subtle green glow border.
optionA.responseScript: You got it! Deep in the Sun's core, hydrogen atoms are crushed together so hard they fuse into helium, releasing incredible amounts of energy. That's what powers all life on Earth!

optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Sun with slight shrinking arrows, question marks floating around. Bold text 'Shrinking?' at bottom. Clean educational style.
optionB.responseScript: Smart observation! Yes, technically the Sun loses mass as it converts matter to energy. But don't worry - it's so massive that it's been doing this for 4.5 billion years and will keep going for another 5 billion!

visual.prompt: Kelly in contemplative, heartfelt pose. Background: Beautiful Earth sunrise from space, golden sunlight streaming across the atmosphere, illuminating clouds and oceans. Life visible on the planet - forests, cities twinkling. Warm golden lighting, cinematic depth of field, emotional atmosphere. Text overlay: 'Our Star Gives Life'. 8K professional photography.
visual.textOverlay: Our Star Gives Life to Everything on Earth
visual.reasoning: Connects the scientific facts to the universal truth - the Sun isn't just a ball of gas, it's the source of all life. Emotional close to cement the learning.

kelly.pose: hands on heart, soft forward lean, genuine warmth
kelly.expression: warm meaningful smile, soft eyes, gentle wisdom
